verses.sanskrit:
भीष्म उवाच।
              एषा प्रथमतो वृत्तिद्वितीयां शृणु भारत। यः कश्चिज्जनयेदर्थं राज्ञा रक्ष्यः सदा नरः॥१॥
verses.english: Bhishma said Do you, O son, O sinless one, listen once more, with feeling of great pride, to the words given vent to by the Island-born Rishi on the subject of the enumeration of the principles. Like a blazing fire, the great Rishi said these words to his son who took after a fire wrapped in smoke. Instructed by what he said, I also, O son, shall again explain to you that certain knowledge.

verses.sanskrit: ह्रियमाणममात्येन भृत्यो वा यदि वा भृतः। यो राजकोशं नश्यन्तमाचक्षीत युधिष्ठिर॥२॥
verses.english: The properties of earth are immobility, weight, hardness, productiveness, scent, density, capacity to absorb all sorts of scents, cohesion, habitableness, and that attribute of the mind which is called patience.

verses.sanskrit: श्रोतव्यमस्य च रहो रक्ष्यश्चामात्यतो भवेत्। अमात्या ह्यपहर्तारो भूयिष्ठं घ्नन्ति भारत॥३॥
राजकोशस्य गोप्तारं राजकोशविलोपकाः। समेत्य सर्वे बाधन्ते स विनश्यत्यरक्षितः॥४॥
verses.english: The properties of water are coolness, taste, moisture, liquidity, softness, agreeableness, tongue, fluidity, capacity to the congealed, and power to melt all earthy products.

verses.sanskrit: अत्राप्युदाहरन्तीममितिहासं पुरातनम्। मुनिः कालकवृक्षीयः कौसल्यं यदुवाच ह॥५॥
verses.english: The properties of fire are irresistible energy, inflammability, heat, capacity to soften, light, sorrow, disease, speed, fury, and upward motion.

verses.sanskrit: कोसलानामाधिपत्यं सम्प्राप्तं क्षेमदर्शिनम्। मुनिः कालकवृक्षीय आजगामेति नः श्रुतम्॥६॥
verses.english: The properties of the wind are touch that is neither hot nor cool, power to help the organs of speech, independence, strength, celerity, power to help all kinds of discharge, power to raise other objects, breaths inhaled and exhaled, life, and birth.

verses.sanskrit: स काकं पञ्जरे बद्ध्वा विषयं क्षेमदर्शिनः। सर्वं पर्यचरद्युक्तः प्रवृत्त्यर्थी पुनः पुनः॥७॥
verses.english: The properties of space are sound, extension, capacity of being enclosed, absence of refuge, power of being unmanifest, capacity for modification, incapacity for resistance, material cause for producing the sense of hearing, and the unoccupied parts of the human body. These are the fifty properties, as declared, which form the essences of the five elementary entities.

verses.sanskrit: अधीध्वं वायसीं विद्यां शंसन्ति मम वायसाः। अनागतमतीतं च यच्च सम्प्रति वर्तते॥८॥
verses.english: Patience, reasoning, remembrance, forgetfulness or error, imagination, endurance, inclination towards good, inclination towards evil, and restlessness,-are the properties of the mind.

verses.sanskrit: इति राष्ट्रे परिपतन्बहुभिः पुरुषैः सह। सर्वेषां राजयुक्तानां दुष्करं परिदृष्टवान्॥९॥
verses.english: Destruction of both good and evil thoughts, perseverance, concentration, decision, and ascertainment of all things depending upon direct evidence, form the five properties of the understanding.

verses.sanskrit: स बुद्ध्वा तस्य राष्ट्रस्य व्यवसायं हि सर्वशः। राजयुक्तापहारांश्च सर्वान्बुद्ध्वा ततस्ततः॥१०॥
verses.english: Yudhisthira said How can the understanding be said to have five properties? How again, can the five senses be described as properties. Explain to me, O grandfather, all this abstruse topic.

verses.sanskrit: ततः स काकमादाय राजानं द्रष्टुमागमत्। सर्वज्ञोऽस्मीति वचनं ब्रुवाणः संशितव्रतः॥११॥
स स्म कौसल्यमागम्य राजामात्यमलंकृतम्। प्राह काकस्य वचनादमुत्रेदं त्वया कृतम्॥१२॥
असौ चासौ च जानीते राजकोशस्त्वया हतः। एवमाख्याति काकोऽयं तच्छीघ्रमनुगम्यताम्॥१३॥
तथाऽन्यानपि स प्राह राजकोशहरांस्तदा। न चास्य वचनं किंचिदनृतं श्रूयते क्वचित्॥१४॥
तेन विप्रकृताः सर्वे राजयुक्ताः कुरूद्वह। तमस्यभिप्रसुप्तस्य निशि काकमवेधयन्॥१५॥
वायसं तु विनिर्भिन्नं दृष्ट्वा बाणेन पञ्जरे। पूर्वाह्ने ब्राह्मणो वाक्यं क्षेमदर्शिनमब्रवीत्॥१६॥
verses.english: Seeing his crow pierced with a shaft within the cage, the twice-born Rishi going to Kshemadarshin in the morning said to hiin,-O king, I seek your help. You are all powerful and you are the lord of the lives and riches of all! If you permit me I can then say what is for your well-bring. Sorry for you whom I regard as a friend, I have come to you, impelled by my devotion and ready to serve you with my whole heart.

verses.sanskrit: राजंस्त्वामभयं याचे प्रभुं प्राणधनेश्वरम्। अनुज्ञातस्त्वया ब्रूयां वचनं भवतो हितम्॥१७॥
मित्रार्थमभिसंतप्तो भक्त्या सर्वात्मनाऽऽगतः। अयं तवार्थो ह्रियते यो ब्रूयादक्षमान्वितः। सम्बुबोधयिषुर्मित्रं सदश्वमिव सारथिः॥१८॥
verses.english: You are being robbed of your wealth, I have come to you for disclosing it without showing any mercy for the robbers. Like a driver that urges a good horse, I have come here for awakening you whom I consider a friend.

verses.sanskrit: तथाविधस्य सुहृदा क्षन्तव्यं स्वं विजानता। ऐश्वर्यमिच्छता नित्यं पुरुषेण बुभूषता॥१९॥
verses.english: The king replied to him, saying,—Why should I not hear anything which you will say, since I am not blind to what is for my good?

verses.sanskrit: तं राजा प्रत्युवाचेदं यत्किंचिन्मां भवान्वदेत्। कस्मादहं न क्षमेयमाकाङ्क्षन्नात्मनो हितम्॥२०॥
verses.english: I grant you permission, O twice-born one! Tell me what you like. I shall certainly obey your instructions, O Brahmana!

verses.sanskrit: ब्राह्मण प्रतिजाने ते प्रब्रूहि यदिहेच्छसि। करिष्यामि हि ते वाक्यं यदस्मान्विप्रवक्ष्यसि॥२१॥
verses.english: The Sage said, Ascertaining the merits and demerits of your servants, as also the dangers which you may meet with at their hands, I have come to you, actuated by my devotion, for informing you of everything.

verses.sanskrit: मुनिरुवाच। ज्ञात्वा पापानपापांश्च भृत्यतस्ते भयानि च। भक्त्या वृत्तिं समाख्यातुं भवतोन्तिकमगमम्॥२२॥
verses.english: His carelessness may create the king's anger, and such anger may bring about his destruction. Carefully learning how to behave himself, one should sit before the king as he should in the presence of a burning fire.

verses.sanskrit: प्रागेवोक्तस्तु दोषोऽयमाचार्यैर्नृपसेविनाम्। अगतीकगतिर्ह्येषा पापा राजोपसेविनाम्॥२३॥
verses.english: The ancient preceptors have declared what the curses are, O king, of those that serve others. The lot of those that serve the king is very miserable and wretched.

verses.sanskrit: आशीविषैश्च तस्याहुः संगतं यस्य राजभिः। बहुमित्राश्च राजानो बह्वमित्रास्तथैव च॥२४॥
verses.english: He who has any connection with kings is said to have connection with snakes of deadly venom. Kings have many friends as also many enemies.

verses.sanskrit: तेभ्यः सर्वेभ्य एवाहुर्भयं राजोपजीविनाम्। तथैषां राजतो राजन्मुहूर्तादेव भीर्भवेत्॥२५॥
verses.english: Those who serve kings have to fear all of them. Every moment, again, they entertain fear from the king himself, O monarch.

verses.sanskrit: नैकान्तेनाप्रमादो हि शक्यः कर्तुं महीपतौ। न तु प्रमादः कर्तव्यः कथंचिद्भूतिमिच्छता॥२६॥
verses.english: A person serving the king cannot escape the charge of carelessness in doing the king's work. Indeed, a servant who desires to acquire prosperity should never show carelessness in the discharge of his duties.

verses.sanskrit: प्रमादाद्धि स्खलेद्राजा स्खलिते नास्ति जीवितम्। अग्निं दीप्तमिवासीदेद्राजानमुपशिक्षितः॥२७॥
verses.english: He should always fear to utter evil words before the king, or to sit cheerlessly or in disrespectful postures, or to walk disdainfully, or to show insolent gestures and disrespectful motions of the limbs.

verses.sanskrit: आशीविषमिव क्रुद्धं प्रभुं प्राणधनेश्वरम्। यत्नेनोपचरेन्नित्यं नाहमस्मीति मानवः॥२८॥
verses.english: Prepared to give up his life itself at every moment, one should serve the king attentively, for the king is all powerful and lord of the lives and the riches of all, and, therefore, like to a snake of deadly venom.

verses.sanskrit: दुर्व्याहृताच्छङ्कमानो दुष्कृताद्दुरधिष्ठितात्। दुरासिताद्दुर्व्रजितादिङ्गितादङ्गचेश्तिात्॥२९॥
verses.english: If the king becomes pleased he can shower prosperity like a god. If he becomes angry he can consume to the very roots like a burning fire.

verses.sanskrit: देवतेव हि सर्वार्थान्कुर्याद्राजा प्रसादितः। वैश्वानर इव क्रुद्धः समूलमपि निर्दहेत्॥३०॥
verses.english: This, O king, was said by Yama. Its truth is seen in the wordly affairs. I shall now do what would increase your prosperity.

verses.sanskrit: इति राजन्यमः प्राह वर्तते च तथैव तत्। अथ भूयांसमेवार्थं करिष्यामि पुनः पुनः॥३१॥
verses.english: Friends like ourselves can give to friends like you the help of their intelligence in times of danger. This crow of mine, O king, has been killed for doing your business.

verses.sanskrit: ददात्यस्मद्विधोऽमात्यो बुद्धिसाहाय्यमापदि। वायसस्त्वेष मे राजन्ननु कार्याभिसंहितः॥३२॥
verses.english: I cannot, however, blame you for this. You are not loved by those who have killed this bird. Ascertain who are your friends and who, your foes. Do everything yourself without handing over your intelligence to others.

verses.sanskrit: न च मेऽत्र भवान्गर्यो न च येषां भवान्प्रियः।  हिताहितांस्तु बुद्ध्येथा मा परोक्षमतिर्भवेः॥३३॥
verses.english: Your establishment consists of all miscreants. They do not seek the well-being of your subjects. I have incurred their hostility.

verses.sanskrit: ये त्वादानपरा एव वसन्ति भवतो गृहे। अभूतिकामा भूतानां तादृशैर्मेऽभिसंहितम्॥३४॥
यो वा भवद्विनाशेन राज्यमिच्छत्यनन्तरम्। आन्तरैरभिसंधाय राजन्सिद्ध्यति नान्यथा॥३५॥
verses.english: Making a conspiration with those servants who can always approach you, they covet the kingdom after destroying you. Their plans, however, have not succeeded owing to unforeseen circumstances.

verses.sanskrit: तेषामहं भयाद्राजन् गमिष्याम्यन्यमाश्रमम्। तैर्हि मे सन्धितो बाणः काके निपतितः प्रभो॥३६॥
verses.english: Through fear of those men, O king, I shall leave this kingdom for some other hermitage. I have no worldly desire, yet those deceitful persons have shot this arrow at my crow, and have, O lord, sent the bird to Yama's abode. I have seen this, O king, with eyes whose vision has been improved by ascetic penances.

verses.sanskrit: छाद्मकामैरकामस्य गमितो यमसादनम्। दृष्टं ह्येतन्मया राजंस्तपोदीर्धेन चक्षुषा॥३७॥
verses.english: With the help of this single crow I have crossed this kingdom of yours that is like a river consisting of alligators, shark, crocodiles and whales.

verses.sanskrit: बहुनक्रझषग्राहां तिमिङ्गिलगणैर्युताम्। काकेन बालिशेनेमां यामतार्षमहं नदीम्॥३८॥
verses.english: Indeed, with the help of that bird, I have passed through your dominions like Himalayan valley, impenetrable and inaccessible for these trunks of (fallen) trees and scattered rocks and thorny shrubs and lions and tigers and other beasts of prey.

verses.sanskrit: स्थाण्वश्मकण्टकवतीं सिंहव्याघ्रसमाकुलाम्। दुरासदां दुष्प्रसहां गुहां हैमवतीमिव॥३९॥
verses.english: The learned hold that a region inaccessible for darkness can be passed through with the a help of a light, and an unfordable river can be crossed by means of a boat. No means, however, exist for penetrating through the labyrinth of royal affairs.

verses.sanskrit: अग्निना तामसं दुर्गं नौभिराप्यं च गम्यते। राजदुर्गावतरणे नोपायं पण्डिता तिदुः॥४०॥
verses.english: Your kingdom is like an inaccessible forest covered with darkness. You cannot trust it. How then can I.

verses.sanskrit: अतो नायं शुभो वासस्तुल्ये सदसती इह। वधो ह्येवात्र सुकृते दुष्कृते न च संशयः॥४२॥
verses.english: For the sake of justice, a person of unrighteous deeds should be killed but never one who is righteous in his deeds. It is not proper, therefore, for one to live in this kingdom long. A sensible man should leave this country soon.

verses.sanskrit: न्यायतो दुष्कृते घातः सुकृते न कथंचन। नेह युक्तं स्थिरं स्थातुं जवेनैवाव्रजेद्बुधः॥४३॥
verses.english: There is a river, O king, of the name of Sita. Boats sink in it. This your kingdom is like that river. An all-destructive net appears to have been cast around it.

verses.sanskrit: सीता नाम नदी राजन्प्लवो यस्यां निमज्जति। तथोपमामिमां मन्ये वागुरां सर्वघातिनीम्॥४४॥
मधुप्रपातो हि भवान् भोजनं विषसंयुतम्। असतामिव ते भावो वर्तते न सतामिव॥४५॥
verses.english: You are like the fall which awaits the collectors of honey, or like attractive food containing poison. Your nature now resembles that of dishonest men and not that of the good. You are like a pit, o king, abounding with snakes of deadly venom.

verses.sanskrit: आशीविषैः परिवृतः कूपस्त्वमसि पार्थिव। दुर्गतीर्था बृहत्कूला कारीरा वेत्रसंयुता॥४६॥
नदी मधुरपानीया यथा राजंस्तथा भवान्। श्व-गृध्र-गोमायुयुतो राजहंससमो ह्यसि॥४७॥
verses.english: You resemble, O king, a river full of sweet water but difficult of access, with steep banks overgrown with Kariras and thorny canes. You are like a swan in the midst of dogs, vultures, and jackals.

verses.sanskrit: यथाऽऽश्रित्य महावृक्षं कक्षः संवर्धते महान्। ततस्तं संवृणोत्येव तमतीत्य च वर्धते॥४८॥
verses.english: Parasites, supported by a huge tree, grow luxuriously, and at last covering the tree itself overshadow it entirely. A forest fire sets in, and catching those grasses first, consumes the tree with them. Thy ministers, O king, resemble those parasites of which I speak, Do you check and correct them.

verses.sanskrit: तेनैवोग्रेन्धनेनैनं दावो दहति दारुणः। तथोपमा ह्यमात्यास्ते राजंस्तान्परिशोधय॥४९॥
त्वया चैव कृता राजन्भवता परिपालिताः। भवन्तमभिसंधाय जिघांसन्ति भवत्प्रियम्॥५०॥
verses.english: They have been nourished by you, But making conspiracy against you, they are destroying your prosperity.

verses.sanskrit: गहनं भवतो राज्यमन्धकारं तमोऽन्वितम्। नेह विश्वसितुं शक्यं भवताऽपि कुतो मया॥५१॥
verses.english: Good and evil are seen here in the same light. To live here is not, therefore, safe. Here a righteous person meets with death, while an unrighteous man incurs no danger.

verses.sanskrit: उषितं शङ्कमानेन प्रमादं परिरक्षता। अन्तः सर्प इवागारे वीरपत्न्या इवालये। शीलं जिज्ञासमानेन राज्ञश्च सहजीविनः॥५१॥
verses.english: Good and evil are seen here in the same light. To live here is not, therefore, safe. Here a righteous person meets with death, while an unrighteous man incurs no danger.

verses.sanskrit: कच्चिज्जितेन्द्रियो राजा कच्चिदस्यान्तरा जिताः। कच्चिदेषां प्रियो राजा कच्चिद्राज्ञः प्रियाः प्रजाः॥५२॥
verses.english: Concealing the faults of your servants, I am living in your palace in constant dread of danger, even like a person living in a room with a snake within it or like the lover of a hero's wife. My object is to ascertain the behaviour of the king who lives with me.

verses.sanskrit: विजिज्ञासुरिह प्राप्तस्तवाहं राजसत्तम। तस्य मे रोचते राजन्क्षुधितस्येव भोजनम्॥५३॥
verses.english: I wish to ascertain whether the king has his passions under restraint, whether his servants obey him, whether he is loved by them, and whether he loves his subjects. For the object of ascertaining all these points, O best of kings, I have come to you.

verses.sanskrit: अमात्या मे न रोचन्ते वितृष्णस्य यथोदकम्। भवतोऽर्थकृदित्येवं मयि दोषो हि तैः कृतः। विद्यते कारणं नान्यदिति मे नात्र संशयः॥५४॥
verses.english: They have found fault with me, because I seek your well-being. I have no doubt that there is no other cause for their hostility to me.

verses.sanskrit: न हि तेषामहं द्रुग्धस्तत्तेषां दोषदर्शनम्। अरेर्हि दुर्हृदाद्भेयं भग्नपुष्ठादिवोरगात्॥५५॥
verses.english: I do not cherish any hostility towards them. I am engaged in only ascertaining their faults. As one should fear a wounded snake, cvery one should fear a wicked foe.

verses.sanskrit: राजोवाच। भूयसा परिहारेण सत्कारेण च भूयसा। पूजितो ब्राह्मणश्रेष्ठ भूयो वस गृहे मम॥५६॥
verses.english: The king said Reside in my abode, O Brahmana. I shall always treat you with respect and honour, and always adore you.

verses.sanskrit: ये त्वां ब्राह्मण नेच्छन्ति ते न वत्स्यन्ति मे गृहे। भवतैव हि तज्ज्ञेयं यत्तदेषामनन्तरम्॥५७॥
verses.english: They that will dislike you shall not live with me. Do you then yourself award what should be their proper sentence.

verses.sanskrit: यथा स्यात्सुधृतो दण्डो यथा च सुकृतं कृतम्। तथा समीक्ष्य भगवन् श्रेयसे विनियुंक्ष्व माम्॥५८॥
verses.english: Do you see, O holy one, then that the rod of punishment is wielded properly and that everything is done well in my kingdom. Reflecting upon everything, do you guide me in such a way that I may acquire prosperity!

verses.sanskrit: मुनिरुवाच। अदर्शयन्निमं दोषमेकैकं दुर्बलीकुरु। ततः कारणमाज्ञाय पुरुषं पुरुषं जहि॥५९॥
verses.english: The sage said Closing your eyes first of all to this offence of theirs, do you weaken them one by one. Prove their faults then and punish them one after another.

verses.sanskrit: एकदोषा हि बहवो मृद्नीयुरपि कण्टकान्। मन्त्रभेदभयाद्राजस्तस्मादेतद्ब्रवीमि ते॥६०॥
verses.english: When many person become guilty of the same offence, they can, by acting in concert, soften the very points of the thorns. Lest your ministers (being suspected, act against you and) disclose your secret counsels, I advise you to proceed cautiously.

verses.sanskrit: वयं तु ब्राह्मणा नाम मृदुदण्डाः कृपालवः। स्वस्ति चेच्छाम भवतः परेषां च यथाऽऽत्मनः॥६१॥
verses.english: As regards ourselves, we are Brahmanas, by nature merciful and reluctant to give pain to any one. We desire your, as well as of others, well-being, even as we wish the good of ourselves.

verses.sanskrit: राजन्नात्मानमाचक्षे सम्बन्धी भवतो ह्यहम्। मुनिः कालकवृक्षीय इत्येवमभिसंज्ञितः॥६२॥
verses.english: I speak of myself, O king! I am your friend. I am known as the sage Kalakavrikshiya.

verses.sanskrit: पितुः सखा च भवतः सम्मतः सत्यसङ्गरः। व्यापन्ने भवतो राज्ये राजन्पितरि संस्थिते॥६३॥
verses.english: Always follow truth. Your father knew me as his friend. When distress overtook this kingdom during the reign of your father, O king, I performed many penances (for driving it off). Leaving off every other business. Out of my affection for you I say this to you so that you may not again commit the fault.

verses.sanskrit: सर्वकामान्परित्यज्य तपस्तप्तं तदा मया। स्नेहात्त्वां तु ब्रवीम्येतन्मा भूयो विभ्रमेदिति॥६४॥
उभे दृष्ट्वा दुःखसुखे राज्यं प्राप्य यदृच्छया। राज्येनामात्यसंस्थेन कथं राजन्प्रमाद्यसि॥६५॥
verses.english: You have obtained a kingdom without any hitch. Think of everything connected with its happiness and misery. You have ministers in your kingdom. But why, O king, should you be guilty of carelessness?

verses.sanskrit: ततो राजकुले नान्दी सञ्जज्ञे भूयसा पुनः। पुरोहितकुले चैव सम्प्राप्ते ब्राह्मणर्षभे॥६६॥
verses.english: After this, the king of Koshala took a minister from the Kshatriya order, and appointed that foremost of Brahmana (viz., the sage Kalakavrikshiya), as his priest.

verses.sanskrit: एकच्छत्रां महीं कृत्वा कौसल्याय यशस्विने। मुनिः कालकवृक्षीय ईजे क्रतुभिरुत्तमैः॥६७॥
verses.english: After these changes had been made, the king of Koshala brought the whole Earth under subjection and acquired great fame. The sage Kalakavrikshiya adored the gods in many grand sacrifices performed for the king.

verses.sanskrit: हितं तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा कौसल्योऽप्यजयन्महीम्। तथा च कृतवान्राजा यथोक्तं तेन भारत॥६८॥
verses.english: Having listened to his wholesome advice, the king of Koshala conquered the whole Earth and acted in every way as the sage directed.
